observations.icon_order: Identical in both images (pixel-diffed the full 560x229 canvas): heaviest → lightest is ↑ arrow (bold solid orange arrowhead) > # hash (medium-weight purple crosshatch) > › chevron (thin, small, same light purple as the hash, clearly the lightest mark on the card).
observations.content_lost: No. Full pixel diff of the two 560x229 images shows differing pixels ONLY in two small regions: y=7-17 (the # glyph) and y=62-71 (the arrow+外部に出る text). Everywhere else — title, 宛先/差出人 rows, message body, 出所 line with the › chevron, and the Cancel/Edit/送る buttons — is byte-for-byte identical between the two files. Nothing present in one is missing from the other.

why.risk_legibility: The ↑ icon and 「外部に出る」 text are pixel-identical in position, size and color (orange) in both images, so noticing the leaves-device warning takes the same effort either way.
why.icon_hierarchy: Since the icons' pixel coverage is the same in both files, the weighting (arrow heaviest, hash medium, chevron lightest) is the same in both — no version does better or worse at matching icon weight to importance.
why.calmness: No visible layout, spacing, or color differences anywhere on the card outside the two glyph regions, so the overall calm/busy impression is the same.
why.visual_craft: I ran a full-canvas pixel diff; the only differing pixels are a ~4% intensity variance in anti-aliasing on the # and ↑ glyphs, with identical foreground-pixel counts in both — consistent with export/rendering noise, not an intentional weight or craft difference I can actually see.
why.overall: By direct pixel comparison the two files are the same design, differing only at a sub-perceptual anti-aliasing level in two small glyph regions; I cannot honestly declare a winner.
